Nightmare Stay: Disgusting Conditions and Dismissive Service

Our two-night stay at OYO Meghna Residency was nothing short of a nightmare. Forced into this establishment due to a last-minute cancellation by another hotel – a cancellation apparently triggered by the lack of an Aadhar card, a baffling requirement for tourists – we were greeted with appalling conditions, dismissive service, and dubious costs.

Despite providing multiple forms of identification, including my license, marriage certificate, and passport, the check-in process was far from smooth. The room we were given reeked of an unpleasant odor, a clear sign of neglect. It seemed deserted, with no other guests in sight during our stay.

The state of the beds and mattresses was abysmal, with visible stains and dirt rendering them unfit for use. When I requested a replacement for the torn bed cover, I was met with resistance from the service staff, who tried to justify the filth rather than rectify it.

Basic amenities like toilet paper and drinking water were luxuries we had to beg for repeatedly. Even when provided, the toilet paper was half-used and clearly recycled. Tap water in a dirty bottle was the closest we got to hydration, a testament to the hotel's disregard for guest comfort and well-being.

In addition to the appalling conditions, the costs incurred were dubious at best. Priced at 1500 INR per night (3000 INR for two nights), the value proposition was abysmal considering the substandard accommodations and lackluster service provided.

To add insult to injury, the receptionist exhibited a shocking level of rudeness and indifference towards our concerns. It became apparent that guest accommodation and satisfaction were not priorities for this establishment.

Even with relatives in the vicinity, we were left to fend for ourselves, as the hotel displayed blatant apathy towards our plight. Constant calls from our relatives were necessary to prompt any semblance of service, highlighting the utter incompetence and neglect rampant at OYO Meghna Residency.

In summary, our experience at OYO Meghna Residency was a harrowing ordeal, marred by unsanitary conditions, indifferent service, and dubious costs. I strongly advise against subjecting oneself to such a dismal establishment, and urge prospective guests to seek accommodations elsewhere for a truly pleasant stay in India.
